speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your vision changes, can you tell me how long you have been noticing the black spots and decreased vision in your right eye? Also, have you experienced any eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and Kaposi's sarcoma, I suspect an opportunistic infection like CMV retinitis. I will order a dilated fundoscopic exam to look for characteristic retinal hemorrhages and exudates. REQUEST TEST: Dilated Fundoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages are classic for Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, especially given your history of AIDS. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other opportunistic infections, I need to check your current immune status. REQUEST TEST: CD4 Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Your CD4 count of 36/mm³ confirms severe immunosuppression, which strongly supports the clinical diagnosis of CMV retinitis given the classic fundoscopic findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis
